dict.string: AVM turns your Mac's VoiceOver off while a macOS virtual machine has the keyboard, so its own VoiceOver gets every key, and back on when you leave it.
AVM lets a virtual machine use your Mac's microphone, when you turn that on in its Settings, for dictation, calls and recordings inside it.
AVM needs local network access so Windows inside your virtual machine can connect to the internet.
AVM needs access to removable drives to store virtual machines on them, and to send them to your Windows virtual machine.
AVM needs USB access to connect peripherals to your Windows virtual machine.
